text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: high-priority page fired for node gpu-178 (kernel panic, kubelet not responding)
incident-bot: Alert details: node=gpu-178, cluster=prod-west, severity=page, summary=kernel panic + kubelet crashloop, triggered by node-exporter heartbeat loss
raj: acked oncall, I'm on it. grabbing serial console access now.
maya: grabbing logs and paging infra. any customer-facing outages reported?
evan: getting customer impact from observability — looks like ~3% of hosted inference qps spiked 500ms errors and ~0.2% 5xx for a small subset of routes pinned to rack-7. Dedicated customers? none affected per RBAC routing.
onchalant : (reaction) :eyes:
sre-lead: good. plan: 1) confirm kernel oops via serial 2) cordon + drain 3) attach serial and try to collect vmcore if possible 4) failover pods and reroute traffic. update PD runbook.
raj: serial console attached. immediate kernel oops visible, stack trace shows "BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference" and GPU driver trace. repeating oops every ~10s.
alex: pv-mounted workload on gpu-178 includes ephemeral scratch. drain should be safe but watch any in-progress batch jobs.
oncall-bot: auto-ack from PagerDuty recorded by raj at 2461209930
maya: starting drain: `kubectl cordon gpu-178 && kubectl drain gpu-178 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force`
--- paste block ---
raj: drain command output: Node gpu-178 cordoned
WARNING: ignoring DaemonSet-managed Pods: kube-proxy, node-exporter
Evicting pod batch-worker-17... evicted
Evicting pod model-server-a... evicted
--- end ---
evan: traffic is rebalancing. 5xx rate dropping but still some tail latency for routes pinned to model-server-a while replicas come up.
platform-eng: I see that NVMe health is good, but kernel oops mentions nvidia. driver version 535.54. i'm pulling dmesg and will attempt a live unload of nvidia modules if safe.
sre-lead: hold on unload until we have crashdump or vmcore; we need forensic. can we trigger kdump?
raj: kdump not configured on this host; serial access to mount remote gdb is possible but timebox to 10m.
alex: customer impact update: small number of hosted apps saw transient 502/504 while pods were rescheduled. no SLA breaches yet but if this persists we may need to open a support ticket for affected customers.
maya: I'm pinging support with a heads-up and the partial customer list.
platform-eng: attempted `rmmod nvidia_drm` results in module busy. can't unload while in use.
raj: doing a soft reboot via IPMI to see if node can land cleanly. IPMI: `ipmitool -I lanplus -H bmc-gpu178 -U admin -P **** chassis power cycle`
incident-bot: IPMI power cycle executed at 2461210450 by raj
raj: node rebooting; serial shows kernel panic during early init, same stack.
evan: traffic fully stabilized after 30s; errors returned to baseline. thanks team.
sre-lead: since kernel panic recurred on boot, mark node as DO NOT BOOT in Fleet for now and move to maintenance. we should isolate and image for deeper analysis.
alex: scheduling replacement: launching reprovision job to reprovision gpu-178 to a known-good image + updated nvidia driver 540.21-rc. will schedule after handoff.
maya: open incident in Jira with notes and attach serial logs. tagging as P2 until replacement complete.
oncall-bot: automatic escalation to secondary oncall (evan) at 2461211200 - evan acknowledged
ev an: taking handoff at 2461211205. summary: kernel panic persists after reboot; node cordoned and drained, traffic recovered. next steps: reprovision node, collect VM core if possible, and run soak test on updated driver image.
sre-lead: agree. also add kernel oops signature to our alerting suppression so we don't get a noisy flood for the same host while we remediate.
raj: capturing a final tarball of `/var/log` and serial dump, uploading to secure S3 path `s3://redwood-incident-dumps/gpu-178/2461209876/`
maya: support notified customers and opened a PSR for the small set of affected customers; tags: "networking, gpu, kernel"
platform-eng: prepping reprovision job: image=prod-gpu-2026-03-10, driver=540.21-rc, enable-kdump=true, post-provision smoke tests: kubelet start, nvml health, model-serving smoke.
evan: leaving a checklist for next oncall: 1) confirm disk encryption keys are accessible after reprovision 2) validate PVC mounts for stateful sets once node rejoins 3) rotate node certificate if unusual fingerprint seen
alex: ETA for reprovision scheduled in 2h from now, will coordinate maintenance window.
sre-lead: good. final status: incident contained, customer impact minimal and transient, node taken out of rotation. transferring to evan for remediation track and follow-up.
maya: documenting RCA stub in incident ticket; will expand after reprovision results.
evan: ack handoff. I'll update thread after reprovision and attach final RCA. thanks everyone for quick triage. :tada:
-- thread ended --
